arml-1997-superrelay-01.title: 3-4-5 triangles
arml-1997-superrelay-01.body:
$\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle CDA$ are right triangles with legs $24,32$ (a $3$-$4$-$5$ shape scaled by $8$), so $AC=40$. The triangle $AEC$ is isosceles ($\angle EAC=\angle ECA$ since the two right triangles are congruent), and $\tan\angle EAC=\frac{DC}{AD}=\frac34$. Its height from $E$ is $h=20\cdot\frac34=15$, so the area is $\frac12\cdot40\cdot15=300$.

**Answer: 300**

arml-1997-superrelay-02.title: Exponentiate
arml-1997-superrelay-02.body:
$K=3$. $\log_2\frac ba=3$ gives $\frac ba=8$, so $b^2=64a^2$ and $b^2-a^2=63a^2$. Hence $M=63$.

**Answer: 63**

arml-1997-superrelay-03.title: Solve the cosine equation
arml-1997-superrelay-03.body:
$K=3$ and $\cos3\theta=\frac12$ gives $3\theta=60^\circ+360^\circ n$ or $300^\circ+360^\circ n$, i.e. $\theta=20^\circ+120^\circ n$ or $100^\circ+120^\circ n$. For $\theta<360^\circ$ the largest is $100^\circ+240^\circ=340^\circ$.

**Answer: $340^\circ$**

arml-1997-superrelay-05.title: Middle term of an AP
arml-1997-superrelay-05.body:
The square has side $9$ and area $81$. If the areas are $\mathrm{II}-d,\ \mathrm{II},\ \mathrm{II}+d$, their sum is $3\,\mathrm{II}=81$, so $\mathrm{II}=27$.

**Answer: 27**

arml-1997-superrelay-07.title: Multiply the equations
arml-1997-superrelay-07.body:
$(abc)^2=T\cdot\frac1T\cdot T^2=T^2$, so $abc=\pm T$ and $c=\frac{abc}{ab}=\pm1$, $a=\frac{T^2}{c}=\pm T^2$. Either way $|a+c|=T^2+1=5$.

**Answer: 5**

arml-1997-superrelay-08.title: Area with a sine
arml-1997-superrelay-08.body:
$AB=15$, $BC=20$, $AC=25$ (a right triangle with the right angle at $B$), $AD=15$. $\sin\angle A=\frac{BC}{AC}=\frac45$, so $[ADB]=\frac12\cdot AB\cdot AD\sin A=\frac12\cdot15\cdot15\cdot\frac45=90$.

**Answer: 90**

arml-1997-superrelay-09.title: Digits
arml-1997-superrelay-09.body:
$K=3$: $27+10A+B=10B+A$, so $9A+27=9B$ and $B=A+3$. The largest two-digit $\underline{BA}$ comes from the largest $B$: $B=9$, $A=6$, giving $\underline{BA}=96$ ($\underline{AB}=69$ and $27+69=96$).

**Answer: 96**

arml-1997-superrelay-10.title: When is y an integer
arml-1997-superrelay-10.body:
$\gcd(5,96)=1$, so $y=\frac{5x}{96}$ is an integer iff $96\mid x$. On $[0,96^2]$ the multiples of $96$ are $0,96,\dots,96\cdot96$: $97$ values.

**Answer: 97**

arml-1997-superrelay-11.title: BD is a diameter
arml-1997-superrelay-11.body:
$K=13$. $BD\perp AC$ at $D$ (median to the hypotenuse of an isosceles right triangle), so the line $BD$ is the perpendicular to $AC$ at the point of tangency $D$; it passes through the centre of $O$. Since $B$ and $D$ are both on the circle and on this line through the centre, $BD$ is a diameter. $BD=\frac12AC=\frac{13\sqrt2}2=\frac{13}{\sqrt2}$, so $a+b=13+2=15$.

**Answer: 15**

arml-1997-superrelay-13.title: Perimeter of the staircase
arml-1997-superrelay-13.body:
$K=115$. Let the smallest side be $x$; the sides are $x,2x,4x,8x$. The perimeter of the staircase is the bottom $15x$, the top edges $15x$, and vertical edges $8x$ on the left (the steps add up to the tallest square's height) and $8x$ on the right: $46x$. So $46x=115$, $x=\frac52$, and the smallest square has area $\frac{25}4$.

**Answer: $\frac{25}4$**

arml-1997-superrelay-14.title: Sale price
arml-1997-superrelay-14.body:
At the sale the price is $0.75K$, which equals $1.2T$. So $K=\frac{1.2}{0.75}T=\frac85T=\frac85\cdot\frac{25}4=10$.

**Answer: 10**

arml-1997-superrelay-15.title: Find the line
arml-1997-superrelay-15.body:
Put $x=1$: $f(2)=2f(0)=2T$. So $(0,T)$ and $(2,2T)$ lie on the line, whose equation is $y=\frac T2x+T$ with intercepts $(0,T)$ and $(-2,0)$. The triangle with the origin has legs $T$ and $2$, area $\frac12\cdot2\cdot T=T=10$. (Check: $f(2x)=Tx+T=2f(x-1)$.)

**Answer: 10**
